concepts.title: Nature of Motivation: Needs, Drives and Goals

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nature of Motivation: Needs, Drives and Goals' refers to.
questions.a: Motivation is the internal process that energises, directs and sustains behaviour toward a goal. It begins with a need -- biological or psychological -- whose arousal creates a drive that pushes the organism into action until the goal reduces the tension. Motivation thus explains both the vigour and the direction of conduct.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nature of Motivation: Needs, Drives and Goals'.
questions.a: Need creates drive, drive fuels action, goal ends it -- motivation is the engine and steering of behaviour.

concepts.title: Types of Motives: Biological and Psychosocial

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Motives: Biological and Psychosocial' refers to.
questions.a: Motives divide into biological needs -- hunger, thirst, sex, sleep -- rooted in the body's requirements, and psychosocial motives learned in society -- achievement, affiliation, power and curiosity. The former are shared with all animals and cycle with the body; the latter vary with culture and individual history.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Motives: Biological and Psychosocial'.
questions.a: Body-built motives and society-taught motives -- hunger pushes everyone, achievement pushes differently.

concepts.title: Nature of Emotions and Their Expression

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nature of Emotions and Their Expression' refers to.
questions.a: Emotions are complex feeling states -- subjective experience, bodily arousal and expressive behaviour together -- that evaluate events as good or bad for us. They are expressed through facial expressions, posture and voice, read widely across cultures, and they energise, direct and even disrupt thought and action.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nature of Emotions and Their Expression'.
questions.a: Emotion is a three-part signal -- felt, aroused and shown -- that appraises the world and mobilises us.
